pairs.subject: subscription-billing-periods
pairs.evidence: app/_lib/billing/plans.ts:194 The allowance recurrence uses billing_state.current_period_start as its anchor. The webhook writer overwrites that value on every renewal (sync.ts:82), and the window end is re-advanced locally (plans.ts:201) instead of read from the provider's currentPeriodEnd. So the 'anchor' is the previous boundary, not durable contract data, and a clamped renewal (31st→28 Feb) can either lose the original day or open an extra allowance key before the provider's next period starts.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/billing/plans.ts:194 The anchor is the provider's rolling current-period start, rewritten each renewal at sync.ts:82 (currentPeriodStart: action.periodStart). No original anchor is persisted, so b[n] is derived from b[n-1]. period-anchor.test.ts:98-103 holds currentPeriodStart fixed, which hides this.

app/_lib/billing/plans.ts:186 Single declared UTC frame: every boundary is built with UTC getters, nothing reads an ambient zone, there is no per-subscriber zone field, and the ledger key is a UTC date. This is the technique's single-zone branch.
app/_lib/billing/plans.ts:169 The boundary input has no zone, and a grep of the billing lib for timezone/timeZone/tz found none. The frame cannot change, so there is nothing to stitch.

app/_lib/billing/sync.ts:183 Periods advance by provider push (event-driven webhooks), not a local recurring pass. Idempotency rides the provider's minted event id, which the technique's 'when not to use' covers.

pairs.registryProposal: anchor-re-derived-not-chained should name a hybrid case. The provider dictates the paid schedule, and the consumer derives a secondary recurrence (an allowance window) from the provider's rolling current-period start. The rule there should be to key the secondary window on the provider's published [start,end) pair, or to persist the original anchor separately. It should not re-advance from the latest ingested start. The 'externally dictated schedules' carve-out currently reads as if this case were exempt.
